youtube.aciklama:
The daily biological check is a visual and listening inspection of the audiometer every morning before the first patient. In this lesson we go step by step through checking cables, earphones and the bone vibrator, comparing with your own thresholds, checking for crosstalk, crackle and noise, and the daily check form.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: ISO 8253-1, Acoustics: Audiometric test methods, Part 1; ANSI/ASA S3.6, Specification for Audiometers; BSA, Recommended Procedure: Pure-tone air-conduction and bone-conduction threshold audiometry; Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology; Gelfand, Essentials of Audiology.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson, we will learn step by step the daily biological check done every morning before the first patient.
We will talk about checking cables, earphones and the vibrator, comparing with your own thresholds, and checking for crosstalk and noise.
A biological check is an inspection of the audiometer by listening to it with the ears of a person with normal hearing.
It is also called a listening check, and it needs no measuring instruments.
The aim is to catch whether the device has developed a fault in daily use, before patients are tested.
The check takes about five minutes; it is done at the start of every test day and whenever the device is moved.

cumleler.yazi: As we saw in the previous lesson, this check corresponds to stage A in ISO 8253-1, that is, routine checks.
cumleler.ses: As we saw in the previous lesson, this check corresponds to stage A in I.S.O. eighty two fifty three, part one, that is, routine checks.

cumleler: A biological check does not replace calibration with measurements, but it safeguards the period between calibrations.

notlar.metin: Right and left in the right channel

cumleler: The check begins with a visual inspection before the device is switched on.
The earphone and vibrator cables are checked for any broken, crushed or frayed sections.
The plugs are checked to be in the correct sockets, with the right earphone in the right channel and the left earphone in the left.
The earphone cushions are checked for cracks or hardening, and the headband for loss of tension.
The patient response button, the intercom and a tight seal of the booth door are also reviewed in this round.
Any noise from the ventilation or from another device in the booth is also noted.
In the listening stage, first put on the earphones and check that the tone comes from both earphones at every frequency.
Listen for clean tones, without crackle or wavering, and confirm that the pitch changes as the frequency changes.
Then place the bone vibrator on your mastoid and listen to the tone at low and mid frequencies.
Switch the masking noise on and off in each earphone to check that it comes from the correct channel.
On the speech channel, try the live microphone and the recorded material player with a short sound.
Finally, confirm that the patient response button and the intercom work in both directions.

notlar.metin: A gap of 10 dB or more: check

cumleler: The strongest part of the check is a person with normal hearing measuring their own thresholds regularly.
When the device has just been calibrated, the checker's thresholds are measured with each earphone and vibrator and recorded as a baseline.
On later days, the same person quickly measures their thresholds, or listens to the tone a little above the baseline threshold.
In this example, today's threshold at four thousand hertz is fifteen decibels worse than the recorded baseline.
In common practice, a difference of ten decibels or more from the baseline calls for a measured check of the device.
First confirm the difference by measuring again; earphone placement or your own condition that day can also play a part.
If the difference persists, the device is not used for patient testing, and the calibration service is called.

maddeler.metin: Is the _sound tube_ kinked or cracked?

cumleler: If your clinic also has insert earphones, the same checks are done with foam tips attached.
With these earphones, the sound tube must not be kinked or cracked; a kinked tube clearly reduces the sound.
Foam tips are single use; a clean tip is used for the check as well.
Sound field loudspeakers are briefly listened to at every frequency at the listening position where the patient sits.
The loudspeakers should not crackle, and the right and left loudspeakers should play from the correct channel.
Crosstalk is the electrical leakage of a signal from one channel into the other channel or earphone.
The active earphone is moved off your head, the other stays on your ear, and a tone, say at seventy dB HL, goes to the active channel.
No sound should be heard in the earphone on your ear; if it is heard, the signal is leaking through the cable or the circuit.
The procedure is repeated for the other side.
Crosstalk can let the test signal reach the opposite ear and distort the results, especially during masking.
With such a finding, the device is sent for service; the problem is often in a cable or connection.

ogeler.metin: As the tone switches on and off

cumleler: After crosstalk, unwanted sounds other than the signal are checked.
Gently move the cables while a tone is playing; crackle, dropouts or level changes point to a cable fault.
No click should be heard as the tone switches on and off; a click can make the patient respond to it instead of the tone.
Listen with the signal off; a buzz or hum suggests electrical noise.
While changing the level in five decibel steps, check that the sound rises and falls smoothly with no extra sound.
Ambient noise in the booth is also roughly checked by ear; we will see its detailed measurement in the next lesson.
The result of the check is marked on a short form every day.
On the form, the cable, earphone and vibrator checks are confirmed one by one.
The difference found when comparing with your own threshold, and the name of the person who did the check, are also written.
The crosstalk, crackle, button and intercom checks also have their own rows.
This form becomes evidence of the days on which the device worked without problems.

sahneler.metin: Have the same person do the check every day, in the same order. Record baseline thresholds right after calibration; small drifts can only be noticed this way.
cumleler: A tip from practice: if possible, have the same person do the check every day, in the same order.
This turns the check into a habit of a few minutes, and no step is skipped.
Record your baseline thresholds right after the device has been calibrated.
If you have a temporary change in hearing, such as a cold, leave the threshold comparison to someone else.

sahneler.baslik: What do you do if you *find a problem?*

maddeler.metin: If it persists: _do not use the device_

yan.metin: No *patient testing* with a doubtful device

cumleler: If you find a problem during the check, first check the connections and settings and repeat the test.
If the problem persists, do not use the device for patient testing, and put a clear note on it.
Write the problem on the form and report it to the technical service.
If it is unclear when the problem started, the results of patients tested since the last successful check can be reviewed.
After repair, the device is not used again until it passes a measured check.
This discipline protects the confidence of both patients and the clinic in the results.

maddeler.metin: A _10 dB_ or larger gap from baseline

cumleler: The biological check is done every day, before the first patient, in about five minutes.
Cables, plugs, earphones and the vibrator are checked first by eye and then by listening.
A difference of ten decibels or more from your own baseline threshold calls for a measured check.
There should be no crosstalk, crackle or clicks; if there is a problem, the device is not used.

sahneler.soru: In the daily check, your 4000 Hz threshold is 15 dB worse than baseline. First step?
sahneler.aciklama: The difference is first confirmed by _measuring again_; if it persists, the device is not used and the service is called.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: In the daily check, your four thousand hertz threshold is fifteen decibels worse than baseline. What is the first step?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: measure again and confirm the difference.
If the difference persists, the device is not used for patient testing; adding a correction or continuing to test is not correct.
